clue.text: Sovereign working in part of spring

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the working piece sits inside the month

parts.note: March is one of the spring months
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A ruler is busy at work during the early weeks of spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a crowned ruler such as a king or queen, a synonym.

clue.text: Vehicle ranked? Try one

parts.note: to try someone's patience is to tax it
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone suggests trying out a vehicle that has been ranked or rated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ranked?' is a playful hint: this vehicle waits at a rank for passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab for hire queues at a rank, so it is a vehicle that is literally ranked.

clue.text: Toy instrument

definitions.meaning: to toy with something is to tinker or play with it idly
a violin, the stringed instrument in folk music

explanation.surface: A small plaything that makes music, like a toy drum.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy is to play idly with fingers, and the folk name for a violin is the same word.

clue.text: Force in garden tool, then cut round it

indicators.note: 'round it' says the cut piece wraps around the tool just named

parts.note: hair or wool that has been cut is shorn
a hoe is a garden tool for weeding

explanation.surface: Instructions for jamming a garden tool in and then trimming around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something into a tight space is to squeeze it in, like using a shoe's aid for a heel.

clue.text: Relief in strong competitors? That was designed to be torture!

definitions.text: That was designed to be torture!

indicators.note: 'in' places the relief piece inside the competitors

parts.note: ironmen are endurance athletes in gruelling triathlons
aid is help or relief

explanation.surface: An endurance race offers relief to tough athletes, though the event seems built to torture them.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a medieval spiked cabinet, a device built to torment its occupant.

clue.text: Note dog's breakfast time

parts.note: a British slang phrase for a mess or muddle
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A reminder that it is time to feed the dog its breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dog's breakfast' is British slang for a shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a short written communication, a synonym.

clue.text: Like that country, a nation in Africa

parts.note: 'so' means in that way, like that
Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: Something is compared to a particular African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is a country in the Horn of Africa, a direct description.

clue.text: Sea found by fish, unusually lucky

indicators.note: 'found by' means the sea piece sits next to the fish piece

parts.note: the char is a freshwater fish related to trout
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: An angler's tale of a fish caught by the sea, an unusually lucky catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmed life is one blessed with uncommon good fortune, as if protected by a spell.

clue.text: Labour leader I greet sadly in job, knocking spirit?

indicators.note: 'in' puts the leader and the rearranged words inside the job

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
sadly suggests the words are in a bad state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A political party's chief greets people gloomily while doing the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' looks like a party chief but just gives the first letter; 'sadly' signals the rearrangement of I GREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost known for banging and rapping noises is a knocking spirit, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One goes either way, as in my gym

definitions.text: One goes either way, as in my gym

parts.words: One goes either way, as in my gym
parts.note: a word or phrase that reads identically forwards and backwards, which 'my gym' does

explanation.surface: Someone describes a route at their gym that runs in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a sequence reads the same in each direction, and the example phrase is one.

clue.text: Food in Salerno, shocking

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A visitor finds the food in an Italian city appalling.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for food or a meal, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Old musician butchers new composition

indicators.note: a new composition of the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A long-dead musician savagely mangles a fresh piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an Austrian composer of the early nineteenth century, an example of an old musician.

clue.text: Guard in bed, suffering complete

indicators.note: suffering suggests the words are in a damaged state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A sentry lies ill in bed, utterly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut text is complete, with nothing shortened or omitted.

clue.text: Colour indigo's sixth on spectrum

indicators.note: the sixth letter of the word indigo is wanted

parts.note: a spectrum is a range of values

explanation.surface: A claim that indigo is the sixth colour of the rainbow, which is true.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites counting colours of the rainbow, but 'sixth' picks the sixth letter of 'indigo', O.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the second hue of the rainbow, an example of a colour.

clue.text: Pineapple, some bananas with syrup, not popular

parts.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas

indicators.note: 'not' says the popular piece is taken out

parts.note: grenadine is a red pomegranate syrup
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A fruit salad recipe: pineapple, a few bananas and syrup, though nobody likes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple is military slang for a small bomb thrown by hand, after its ridged shape.

clue.text: Magic! That will bring the house down

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of delight meaning brilliant or terrific

definitions.text: That will bring the house down
definitions.meaning: an explosive that would demolish a building, punning on a show bringing the house down

explanation.surface: A conjuring act so good the audience will cheer the theatre down.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for terrific and literally an explosive that demolishes buildings.

clue.text: Wheels off in plant

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
to be off is to be away

explanation.surface: A car drives away and the wheels come off inside a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a herb of the parsley family grown for its seeds, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Doctor sharing extra food

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician shares out second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative addition such as parsley on a plate is an extra bit of food.

clue.text: Unproductive mogul, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: this phrase says a word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a mogul or tycoon is a business baron

explanation.surface: A query whether a business tycoon is getting nothing done.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land yields no crops, so it is unproductive, a synonym.

clue.text: European college student welcoming recess, finally

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: an Etonian attends Eton College, the English public school

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A student from the continent is welcomed at a college during the holiday break.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from a Baltic state is an example of a European.

clue.text: Kid brother's heart in China?

parts.note: to kid is to tease

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A little brother's heart is in a faraway country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China?' is not the country: china is porcelain, and the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cups and saucers made of porcelain is an example of china.

clue.text: Joker, say, witty type

definitions.meaning: the joker is an example of a playing piece in a pack
an amusing, eccentric person is called this informally

explanation.surface: A joker is described as a funny sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: The joker is one in a pack of playing pieces, and a comic person is also informally so called.

clue.text: Strange sap on cream cheese

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An odd tree sap is spread over a creamy cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a soft Italian cheese used in tiramisu, an example of cheese.

clue.text: Catch up and split up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to catch is to trap

explanation.surface: Two people meet to catch up, then go their separate ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to separate or split up, a synonym.

clue.text: Vulgar woman partly regretted always being laid back

indicators.note: laid back means the chosen letters run backwards
partly says only a part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A coarse woman has some regrets but always stays relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a young woman who behaves in a loud, boozy, laddish way.

clue.text: Most within range are in tree-house

indicators.note: 'in' places the word are inside the tree-house

parts.note: a bird's nest is a home in a tree

explanation.surface: Most children within reach are playing in the tree-house.
explanation.definitionFit: The closest thing is the one most within reach or range, a superlative synonym.
